## This game

A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll read game 119 and the position helper, then play at 20k while focusing on earlier development and protecting room for life before walls form.

G5 replaced the usual early E5 central stone. D3/E3 connected the left, G4 physically joined G3/G5, and F3 joined ALL lower/right stones. These joins were useful and correctly counted.
But G6 was taken FIRST while Black played C2/B2. H6 was SEPARATE three H5/H7/J6; actual H7 closed the upper route, H5 joined main, J7 capped the edge. The stated plan to expand around G6 failed immediately. H6 was not a forced route to the upper-right.
Review BEFORE D3/E3/G4/F3 and C2/B2/G6: connecting and defending left consumed the time needed for right expansion. Earlier G6 or an upper foothold is an UNTESTED review alternative, not a proven winning move.

## Failed left entry
C7 was first played at23, after the right cap, without a credible two-eye plan against the FIRST reply C8. C6 answered C8 downward, but D7 closed east. C5 expanded downward but D5 joined the WHOLE White wall. B7 expanded west but B8 closed the top.
Four Black stones B7/C5/C6/C7 had A7/B5/B6, all enemy-facing, no eyes. A5 was inspected as a separate three-liberty candidate but not played. Manual reading found that hostile cuts/edge closure could still eliminate life; no exhaustive death or rescue proof is claimed.
The whole left allocation was withdrawn verbally before G8. White B5 left A7/B6, A7 left sole B6, and B6 captured four at60. B6 extension would only add blockable A6 while B5/A7 prevent life; not played.
Review belongs BEFORE C7/C8 and C6/D7, not at final atari. Late footholds and serial healthy-looking liberties repeated the familiar losing pattern.

## Actual top rescue
G8 was a separate four-liberty entry at31. G7 joined White F7/G6/H7/J7, closing below. F8 connected west but E8 blocked it. H8 connected east.
Crucially White J6 then J5 spent two moves BELOW the top, allowing Black J8 to physically join and secure the upper-right edge. F9 joined F8 and separated actual upper region G9/H9/J9 from outside E9. White E9 blocked outside.
H9 ACTUALLY joined H8/J8 and split private G9 and J9. Both have ONLY Black orthogonal borders. Whole six has two liberties, both genuine single-point eyes. Do not fill either.
This rescue worked against actual replies. It does NOT prove the entry or F8/H8 extensions survive FIRST hostile occupation of J8 or the required eye separator. I discussed these restrictive replies manually; no exhaustive successful response was established. The strategic gate was still incomplete, despite actual success.

## Lower closure and actual separators
H3 connected through G3 against J3, but White J4 joined the whole right wall. H2/H1 were connected replies to J2; White gained Jfile down to J1.
White A2 entered before the left-bottom closure. B1 joined main and sealed the bottom; White J1 elsewhere allowed A1, joined through B1, atariing A2. Actual A3 joined A2 to the whole left wall. No capture.
H4 and F4 each gained an actual mixed point with ZERO new liberties; whole lower chain remained healthy. They were useful outside gains, not life by themselves.
E2 alone did NOT separate the bottom region. E1 ACTUALLY split C1/D1/D2 (three) from F1/F2/G1/G2 (four), same chain. D1 then joined through E1 and split private C1/D2, preserving the right four-point region. Two private single-point eyes secure the lower chain independently of the uninvaded four-point region.

Black TWO chains: upper six+G9/J9 two=8; lower21+C1/D2 two+F1/F2/G1/G2 four=27. Total27 stones+eight empties=35.
White SEVEN chains,31 stones+15 exclusive empties=46. Empty regions: B9/C9/D8/D9 four,A8 one,B7/C5/C6/C7 four,A4/A5/A6 three,E7 one,F6 one,E5 one.
35 versus46+7 gives W+18 exactly. No mixed regions or dead-stone assumptions; all remaining Black groups have private eyes. Pass63/pass64 completed.
No maintained coordinate pointset, credible early winning allocation, full per-move area audit, exhaustive rescue proof, or optimal-pass claim.

Read this review before game120. Stay20k.
Keep actual G4/F3 joins, whole-enemy join checks, H9 protecting G9/J9, zero-new-liberty outside gains in healthy groups, and E1/D1 separators protecting C1/D2.
Change development BEFORE G6 caps the right and BEFORE C7/C8 repeats unsupported late entry. Supported expansion in118 did not transfer simply by moving G5 earlier. A connected lower group and one rescued eight-point top group still total only35.

Rules: Chinese area, komi 7, simple ko, no suicide. User's current instructions govern each game. Play through a result and save lessons and SGF before ending the session. Tools and analysis code may inspect the current board, count liberties and check legality; never build/use an engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search, or a program recommending/ranking moves.

Critical improvement: count DISTINCT liberties of ALL endangered friendly groups before each move. Joining groups does not guarantee safety. Check again after selecting a move, especially if it fills a friendly liberty. Game 1 lost six connected stones because the sole liberty J4 was overlooked. Use current-position-liberties.js as a counting aid, not as a move selector.

Before tenuki, identify opponent's immediate captures and cuts. Treat groups with one liberty as emergencies and two liberties as tactical concerns. Near the first line, assess escape routes before attaching: F8 in game 1 became trapped after F7/G8, and chasing along row 9 did not create an escape.

Do not describe groups as alive, connected safely, or enemy stones as dead without checking actual liberties and eye space. Distinguish observations from unverified strategic impressions.

Game 2 improvement: liberty counting alone is insufficient. Check actual eye space and an exit before enclosure. W34 D8 joined the upper group but left two liberties and no established eyes. Running F9/G9/H9 kept two liberties without escaping. Capturing C8 with C7 created only one eye; B45 J9 left 17 White stones with sole liberty C8, which White could not fill legally. An enemy stone in atari does not establish friendly life. Avoid filling interior space merely to connect.

B39 B4 kept three liberties without establishing eyes. A5/A6 repeated edge running; W44 A7 left seven stones with sole liberty A4. The main right chain had ten liberties, but controlling that side was insufficient. Assess rough area balance earlier, and reassess an invasion when replies remove its living space. Liberty counts describe danger; they do not establish a rescue.

But W42 H3 entered the lower right without naming two usable eye regions. B43 H2 blocked the bottom route; B51 F6 joined the enclosing Black chains. At the end, eight White stones had {G3,J1,J4,J5,J6}; G3/J1/J6 bordered Black stones and were not enclosed eyes, while adjacent J4/J5 formed one region. Identify two potential eye regions before an isolated entry, check which replies remove them, and reassess immediately when they disappear. Roughly 32 White area plus komi was insufficient if Black controlled the rest; assess balance before needing a late isolated group.

But B29 C5 cut with only {B5,C6}, no eye, and an incorrect capture expectation. W30 B5 gained B6, leaving White {A5,B6}, while C5 was in atari at C6. store("inspect",`(s,m)=>{const c='ABCDEFGHJ',b={};for(const l of s.split('\\n')){const a=l.match(/^\\s*([1-9])\\s+([XO.](?:\\s+[XO.]){8})\\s+[1-9]/);if(a)a[2].split(/\\s+/).forEach((v,i)=>b[c[i]+a[1]]=v)}const n=p=>[[c.indexOf(p[0])-1,+p[1]],[c.indexOf(p[0])+1,+p[1]],[c.indexOf(p[0]),+p[1]-1],[c.indexOf(p[0]),+p[1]+1]].filter(([x,y])=>x>=0&&x<9&&y>0&&y<10).map(([x,y])=>c[x]+y);const groups=()=>{let seen=new Set(),g=[];for(const p in b){if(seen.has(p)||b[p]=='.')continue;let st=[],li=new Set(),q=[p];seen.add(p);while(q.length){let t=q.pop();st.push(t);for(const v of n(t)){if(b[v]=='.')li.add(v);else if(b[v]==b[p]&&!seen.has(v)){seen.add(v);q.push(v)}}}g.push({color:b[p],stones:st.sort().join(' '),liberties:[...li].sort().join(' '),count:li.size})}return g};const before=groups();let captured=[];if(m){if(b[m]!='.')throw Error('occupied');b[m]='O';for(const g of groups())if(g.color=='X'&&!g.count){for(const p of g.stones.split(' ')){b[p]='.';captured.push(p)}}}const after=groups();let seen=new Set(),regions=[];for(const p in b){if(b[p]!='.'||seen.has(p))continue;let q=[p],pts=[],border=new Set();seen.add(p);while(q.length){let t=q.pop();pts.push(t);for(const v of n(t)){if(b[v]!='.')border.add(b[v]);else if(!seen.has(v)){seen.add(v);q.push(v)}}}regions.push({points:pts.sort().join(' '),border:[...border].sort().join('')})}return {before,selected:m?after.find(g=>g.stones.split(' ').includes(m)):null,captured,regions,after}}`);
